problems.title: Parity narrows a positive integer equation
problems.question: Count positive integer pairs solving 2x+3y=23.
problems.idea: y must be odd.
steps: The allowed positive odd y are 1,3,5,7.
Their x-values are 10,7,4,1.

problems.title: Factor denominators before evaluating
problems.question: Evaluate [a²/(a+n)-a³/(n²+2an+a²)]·[a/(a+n)+a²/(n²-a²)]⁻¹ at a=2.5,n=-1.5.
problems.idea: Simplify each bracket separately.
steps: The first bracket is a²n/(a+n)².
The second is an/[(n+a)(n-a)].
Dividing gives a(n-a)/(a+n) on the original domain.
The given inputs are valid and give 2.5·(-4)/1=-10.

problems.title: Separate constants in a rational equation
problems.question: Solve (3x-5)/(x-1)-(2x-5)/(x-2)=1.
problems.idea: Exclude x=1,2 first.
steps: The constants cancel against the right side, leaving 1/(x-2)=2/(x-1).
Thus x-1=2x-4 and x=3, which is allowed.

problems.title: Sharp bounds on a difference of reciprocals
problems.question: Find the range of X=1/a-2/b if 1<a<2,3<b<4.
problems.idea: Invert each positive interval.
steps: The least possible limiting difference is 1/2-2/3=-1/6.
The greatest limiting difference is 1-1/2=1/2.
Neither endpoint is attained, and independent continuous inputs give every intermediate value.
problems.note: The looser printed bounds -1/3<X<1/2 and -1/6<X<3/2 are also true. The answer above is the exact range, rather than just a valid estimate.

problems.title: Square a reciprocal sum
problems.question: Find (a⁴+b⁴)/(a²b²) if a/b+b/a=3.
problems.idea: Square the given equation.
steps: Thus the requested sum is 9-2=7, with a,b≠0.

problems.title: Opposite exponents cancel
problems.question: Simplify [(a⁻³b⁻³)/(a⁻⁴b⁻²)]⁻¹⁹⁹·[(a⁻⁴b⁻⁶)/(a⁻⁵b⁻⁵)]¹⁹⁹.
problems.idea: Both inner quotients are the same.
steps: Each bracket simplifies to a/b.
Their exponents -199 and 199 sum to zero.

problems.title: Add daily food consumption
problems.question: A chicken eats 1 kg in 9 days, a duck in 6, a goose in 2. How long does 100 kg feed 4 chickens,5 ducks,3 geese?
problems.idea: Add the kilograms consumed per day.

problems.title: Three units-digit cycles
problems.question: Find the last digit of 199¹⁹⁹+2017²⁰¹⁷-2017¹⁹⁹.
problems.idea: Reduce the bases modulo 10.
steps: The total units residue is 9+7-3=13≡3.

problems.title: A linear denominator divides a prime remainder
problems.question: For how many integers a is (16a²+8a+200)/(4a+1) an integer?
problems.idea: Complete the numerator around the denominator square.
steps: 199 is prime, so the possible denominator values are ±1,±199.
It must also be 1 modulo 4. Only 1 and -199 satisfy that condition.
These give a=0 and a=-50.

problems.title: Purchasing power is salary divided by price
problems.question: Salary falls 10% while product price rises 20%. What percentage fewer units can the salary buy?
problems.idea: Divide the two percentage multipliers.
steps: The loss of purchasing quantity is 1/4.

problems.title: Two perimeters in an isosceles trapezoid
problems.question: In isosceles trapezoid ABCD, bases BC,AD and altitude BH, quadrilateral ABCH has perimeter 12. Find perimeter DCH.
problems.idea: The equal overhangs replace two boundary segments.
steps: ABCH has perimeter AB+BC+CH+HA.
DCH has perimeter DC+CH+HD.
Using the two displayed equalities makes those perimeter sums identical.

problems.title: Midpoints of trapezoid diagonals
problems.question: A right trapezoid has acute angle 60° and slanted leg 20. Find the distance between diagonal midpoints.
problems.idea: It is half the difference of the bases.
steps: Half of 10 is 5.

problems.title: A split midline determines base ratio
problems.question: Trapezoid diagonals meet midline MN at K,P, with K between M,P and MK:KP=2:3. Find the base ratio.
problems.idea: Use the standard three midline pieces.
steps: Thus b/(B-b)=2/3.
Write b=2t,B-b=3t, giving B=5t.

problems.title: Altitude rays versus altitude lines
problems.question: A parallelogram has acute angle 75°. Find the angle between the two altitude rays from that vertex.
problems.idea: One altitude ray points outside the parallelogram.
formulas: If adjacent side directions are 0°,75°, the altitude directions are 90°,-15°.
steps: Their ray separation is 90°-(-15°)=105°.
The acute angle between the complete altitude lines would be 75°, but the two drawn altitude segments give the supplementary angle.

problems.title: Two adjacent bisectors meet on the opposite side
problems.question: In parallelogram MNPQ, the M,Q bisectors meet at K on NP. The circumradius of triangle MKQ is 3.3. Find parallelogram perimeter.
problems.idea: Adjacent internal bisectors are perpendicular.
formulas: MQ is the hypotenuse of MKQ, so MQ=2R=6.6.
steps: The bisector and parallel-side angle equalities give NK=MN and KP=PQ.
Hence NP=MN+PQ=2MN. Since NP=MQ=6.6, MN=3.3.
The perimeter is 2(6.6+3.3)=19.8.

problems.title: Only the two specified sides change
problems.question: One rhombus side increases 30% and another increases 50%. Find the percentage perimeter increase.
problems.idea: The other two sides retain their lengths.
steps: The increase is 0.8s out of 4s, or 20%.
problems.note: This changes one side by each stated percentage. Changing both pairs of opposite sides would be a different instruction.

problems.title: Perimeter of a triangle cut off by a tangent
problems.question: A is distance a from a circle centre. Two tangents AB,AC make angle 120°. A further tangent on minor arc BC cuts AB,AC at M,N. Find perimeter AMN.
problems.idea: Equal tangent lengths make the corner perimeter twice AB.
steps: If the new contact is T, MT=MB and NT=NC.
Thus AM+AN+MN=AB+AC=2AB=a.

problems.title: Midpoints need not form a rectangle
problems.question: M,N,K,P are consecutive side midpoints of a quadrilateral. Which listed assertion is false?
problems.idea: Varignon’s theorem guarantees a parallelogram.
formulas: Each midpoint side is parallel to one original diagonal.
steps: It can be a rectangle, rhombus or square for suitable original diagonals.
It is not necessarily a rectangle: this would require the original diagonals to be perpendicular.
problems.answer: “It is necessarily a rectangle” is false.

problems.title: A projection ratio needs an order
problems.question: In rectangle ABCD, the perpendicular from B splits diagonal AC in ratio 1:3. The diagonal intersection is distance a from side AD. Find the diagonal length.
problems.idea: AB is twice the given centre-to-side distance.
formulas: AB=2a; AB²:BC²=AH:HC for altitude foot H on AC.
steps: If AH:HC=1:3, then BC=√3AB and AC=2AB=4a.
If the unnamed two pieces are instead in the reverse order, BC=AB/√3 and AC=2AB/√3=4a/√3.
The listed answer 4a assumes the first ordering.
problems.answer: 4a for AH:HC=1:3; 4a/√3 for the reversed ordering.
problems.note: The source gives the ratio without naming its order, so both configurations satisfy the literal statement.

problems.title: How many convex angles can be acute?
problems.question: Find the greatest number of acute interior angles in a convex polygon.
problems.idea: Each acute interior angle requires an exterior turn exceeding 90°.
formulas: Exterior turns of a convex polygon sum to 360°.
steps: Four acute interior angles would require more than 360° of exterior turn, impossible.
Three are attainable in any acute triangle.

problems.title: Squaring an interval that crosses zero
problems.question: Find the range of Y=(2a-b)² if 1<a<2,3<b<4.
problems.idea: First bound the inner linear expression.
steps: The inner expression can equal zero, so the least square is 0 and is attained.
Its largest absolute limiting value is 2, not attained, so the squared range ends below 4.

problems.title: Cancellation gives a contradiction
problems.question: Solve x+1-(x-x²)/(1-x)=0.
problems.idea: Retain x≠1 before cancelling.
steps: On the domain the equation becomes x+1-x=0, or 1=0.
There is no allowed solution.

problems.title: An integer linear combination has a divisibility condition
problems.question: For which listed a does 8x+4y=a have integer solutions?
problems.idea: The left side is always divisible by 4.
formulas: gcd(8,4)=4; an integer solution exists iff 4 divides a.
steps: Conversely, if a=4k, choose x=0,y=k.
Among the printed values 1,2,3,4, only 4 qualifies.
problems.answer: a=4 among the choices; generally every multiple of 4.

problems.title: Cancel a factored difference of squares
problems.question: Simplify 4a/(4a²-b²)+1/(b-2a).
problems.idea: Express both denominators using 2a-b.
steps: The common numerator is 4a-(2a+b)=2a-b.
Cancel to obtain 1/(2a+b), retaining b≠±2a.

problems.title: A nested fraction collapses from the inside
problems.question: Simplify 1+1/[1-1/(1+1/x)].
problems.idea: Start with the deepest denominator.
steps: Taking its reciprocal gives x+1, and adding 1 gives x+2.
The original restrictions are x≠0,-1.
